tagline: Terminal client for Nextloom — manage your profile, track applications, and generate documents, without leaving the terminal.

install.summary: Install with one command. Downloads the right binary for your platform, no Node or Bun required.
install.note: Installs a standalone ~55 MB binary (it bundles its own runtime) to ~/.nextloom/bin and adds it to your PATH. Both `nextloom` and the shorter `nai` are installed and behave identically. You can also download a binary manually from the GitHub Releases page.

sections.title: Auth
sections.description: Sign in and manage your session.

commands.name: nextloom auth login
commands.description: Opens your browser to sign in with Clerk, then stores a local session token at ~/.config/nextloom/auth-<env>.json (permissions 0600) — one file per environment, so a dev session never overrides a prod one.
examples:
nextloom auth login

  Opening your browser to sign in...
  Waiting for the callback...
  Signed in as ada@example.com.

nextloom auth login --json

  {"ok":true,"email":"ada@example.com"}

commands.name: nextloom auth logout
commands.summary: Revoke and clear the local session.
commands.description: Revokes the stored token and deletes the current environment's session file (~/.config/nextloom/auth-<env>.json). Other environments are left signed in.
examples:
nextloom auth logout

  Signed out.

nextloom auth logout --json

  {"ok":true}

commands.name: nextloom auth whoami
commands.description: Prints the currently authenticated user. With --json, emits the issuer's userinfo response unchanged, so it carries more fields than the human view shows.
examples:
nextloom auth whoami

  Ada Lovelace
  ada@example.com
  id: user_2xKkLmNpQrStUvWx

nextloom auth whoami --json

  {
    "object": "oauth_user_info",
    "instance_id": "ins_2xKkLmNpQrStUvWx",
    "user_id": "user_2xKkLmNpQrStUvWx",
    "sub": "user_2xKkLmNpQrStUvWx",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "email_verified": true,
    "family_name": "Lovelace",
    "given_name": "Ada",
    "name": "Ada Lovelace",
    "picture": "https://img.clerk.com/example"
  }

commands.name: nextloom profile edit
commands.description: Set fields by their dotted path. Run `nextloom profile view --path` to list every path and its current value. Values are read-modify-write: the whole field group is re-sent with your change applied, so untouched fields keep their values. JSON array and object values are parsed.

flags.name: --field
flags.description: Set a field non-interactively. Repeatable.

examples:
nextloom profile edit --field personalInfo.timezone=America/Chicago

  Updated personalInfo.timezone: America/Los_Angeles → America/Chicago

nextloom profile edit --field workPreferences.workMode='["remote","onsite"]'

  Updated workPreferences.workMode: ["remote"] → ["remote","onsite"]

nextloom profile edit --field personalInfo.address.city=Austin --field personalInfo.address.state=Texas

  Updated personalInfo.address.city: Houston → Austin
  Updated personalInfo.address.state: → Texas

nextloom profile edit --field personalInfo.timezone=America/Chicago --json

  {"ok":true,"changes":[{"path":"personalInfo.timezone","from":"America/Los_Angeles","to":"America/Chicago"}]}

commands.name: nextloom profile skill list
commands.summary: List your skills, grouped by category.
commands.description: Lists the skills on your profile, grouped by the category the skill taxonomy assigns. Skills that matched nothing in the taxonomy are grouped under "Other". With one category, or none, the grouping is dropped and the skills are listed plainly.
examples:
nextloom profile skill list

  Cloud            AWS · Fly.io · Vercel
  Databases        Cassandra · MySQL · PostgreSQL
  DevOps           CI/CD · Docker · Jenkins · Kubernetes
  Languages        C · Go · Java · Python · SQL · TypeScript
  ML               AI · Generative AI · LLM · LangChain
  Other            ai agents · api design · llms

nextloom profile skill list --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.category=="language") | .display_name'

  C
  Go
  Java

nextloom profile skill list

  No skills on your profile.

commands.name: nextloom profile skill add
commands.description: Adds a skill to your profile. The name is matched against the skill taxonomy, so the stored skill may be the canonical spelling rather than exactly what you typed. Adding one you already have changes nothing.
examples:
nextloom profile skill add TypeScript

  Added "TypeScript".

nextloom profile skill add typescript --json

  {"ok":true,"matched":true,"skill":"TypeScript"}

commands.name: nextloom profile skill remove
commands.description: Removes a skill from your profile, matching the name case-insensitively. Removing one you do not have is not an error.
examples:
nextloom profile skill remove TypeScript

  Removed "TypeScript".

nextloom profile skill remove Fortran

  "Fortran" was not on your profile.

nextloom app list

commands.name: nextloom app add
commands.description: Creates a job application from a job posting and imports it in one step. The job description text is required (--file, or --file - for stdin): Nextloom does not fetch job pages, so a URL on its own cannot be imported — scrape the posting first and pass the text. Company name and job title are extracted from that text by AI, the same way the web app does it; you do not type them. --url is optional and stores the link alongside the record.

flags.name: --file
flags.description: Job description text file. Use - to read it from stdin. Required.

flags.name: --url
flags.description: Job posting URL, stored with the record. Optional, and never fetched — it does not replace --file.

flags.name: --applied-date
flags.description: When you applied (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

flags.name: --wait
flags.description: Wait for AI to extract the company and title. --no-wait returns as soon as it is created.

examples:
nextloom app add --file jd.txt --url https://acme.example/jobs/42

  # the usual case: you scraped the posting, so pass the text and the link
  Created application app_a1b2c3
  app_a1b2c3             New             71%  2026-08-01  Acme Corp

nextloom app add --file jd.txt

  # no link to store — a description from an email, a PDF, or a paste
  Created application app_d4e5f6
  app_d4e5f6             New             64%  2026-08-01  Acme Corp

nextloom app add --file -

  # reads the posting piped on stdin: pbpaste | nextloom app add --file -
  Created application app_g7h8i9
  app_g7h8i9             New            100%  2026-08-01  Initech

nextloom app add --url https://acme.example/jobs/42

  Error: Missing required flag "--file"

  # a URL on its own is never imported: nothing fetches the page, so the
  # record would stay empty forever. Scrape the posting text first.

nextloom app add --file jd.txt --no-wait

  Created application app_j1k2l3
  app_j1k2l3             New               —  2026-08-01  —
  Still extracting. Check again with: nextloom app view app_j1k2l3

nextloom app add --file jd.txt --applied-date 2026-01-15 --json

  {"id":"app_a1b2c3","company_name":"Acme Corp","status":"New","applied_date":"2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z"}

commands.name: nextloom app update
commands.description: Updates the status of an existing application.

flags.name: --status
flags.description: The new status. Valid: New, Applied, Screening, Interviewing, Offered, Declined, Accepted, Withdrawn, Archived.

commands.name: nextloom app delete
commands.description: Permanently deletes a job application. On a terminal it shows you the application and asks to confirm. Anywhere it cannot ask — a pipe, a script, or --json — it refuses unless you pass --force.

flags.name: --force
flags.description: Delete without asking. Required in scripts and with --json.

examples:
nextloom app delete app_a1b2c3

  ID                     STATUS        MATCH  APPLIED     COMPANY
  app_a1b2c3             New             87%  2026-06-20  Acme Corp

  Delete this application? [y/N] y
  Deleted app_a1b2c3.

nextloom app delete app_a1b2c3

  ID                     STATUS        MATCH  APPLIED     COMPANY
  app_a1b2c3             New             87%  2026-06-20  Acme Corp

  Delete this application? [y/N]
  Cancelled. Nothing was deleted.

nextloom app delete app_a1b2c3 --force

  Deleted app_a1b2c3.

nextloom app delete app_a1b2c3 --json

  {"error":"Refusing to delete app_a1b2c3 without confirmation. Nothing here can prompt (not a terminal, or --json), so pass --force."}

nextloom app delete app_a1b2c3 --force --json

  {"id":"app_a1b2c3","deleted":true}

sections.title: Resume
sections.description: Manage your master resume — the foundation for all generated documents.

commands.name: nextloom resume view
commands.description: Prints your master resume fields (personal info, work experience, education, skills, certifications).
examples:
nextloom resume view

  PERSONAL
    Full name     Ada Lovelace
    Email         ada@example.com
    Summary       Full-stack engineer with 8 years of experience...

  WORK EXPERIENCE
    1. Senior Engineer — Acme Corp (2020–2026)
       Led the platform team...

  EDUCATION

nextloom resume view --json

  {"personal_info":{"full_name":"Ada Lovelace","email":"ada@example.com",...}}

commands.name: nextloom resume export
commands.summary: Export your resume as markdown or JSON.
commands.description: Downloads your master resume in the requested format.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Output format. Default: md.

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Where to save the file. Default: stdout.

examples:
nextloom resume export --format md

  # Ada Lovelace
  Full-stack engineer...

nextloom resume export --format json --output ./resume.json

  Saved resume to ./resume.json

commands.name: nextloom resume import
commands.description: Uploads a resume file (.txt, .md, .docx, .pdf) and waits for the backend to parse it. The parsed fields become your master resume.

flags.name: --wait
flags.description: Wait for parsing to complete (default: true).

examples:
nextloom resume import ./resume.pdf

  Uploading resume.pdf...
    ✓ Processing                    29s
  Resume imported successfully.

nextloom resume import ./resume.pdf --no-wait

  Import queued (job job_x1y2z3).

sections.title: Documents
sections.description: Generate, list, and download the documents for an application. Generating runs an AI pipeline and replaces what was there; downloading only reads.

commands.name: nextloom doc generate
commands.summary: Generate a document for an application.
commands.description: Runs the AI pipeline for a document type, waits for it, and downloads the result. This replaces any existing document of that type and consumes quota — to fetch one you already have, use `doc get`. Resumes run five steps (benchmark, tailor, ATS check, humanize, final check) and cover letters three; follow-ups and thank-you notes are single-shot. A resume may loop back to tailoring when the ATS check rejects a draft, which shows as a retry. The CLI streams progress and downloads the file before returning, so do not poll. Saved files use the same name the web app downloads them under — <Your_Name>_Resume_<Company>.<ext> — so the two do not diverge.

args.name: type
args.description: Document type: resume, cover-letter, follow-up, or thank-you.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Output format. Resume and cover letter: md, json, docx, pdf. Follow-up and thank-you: json.

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Where to save the file. Defaults to the name the web app would give it.

examples:
nextloom doc generate resume app_a1b2c3 --format pdf --output ./resume.pdf

  Generating resume for app_a1b2c3 (job job_x1y2z3)...
    ✓ Queued                          1s
    ✓ 1/5  Benchmarking               8s
    ✓ 2/5  Tailoring                 19s
    ✓ 3/5  ATS check                 24s
    ✓ 4/5  Humanizing                52s
    ✓ 5/5  Final check               58s
  Saved resume to ./resume.pdf

nextloom doc generate resume app_a1b2c3

  # Tailoring repeats when the ATS check rejects the draft, which is why a
  # generation can take well over a minute.
  Note: a resume already exists for this application. Regenerating replaces it and uses quota.
  Generating resume for app_a1b2c3 (job job_x1y2z3)...
    ✓ Queued                          1s
    ✓ 1/5  Benchmarking               8s
    ✓ 2/5  Tailoring                 19s
    ✓ 3/5  ATS check                 24s
    ✓ 2/5  Tailoring (retry 2)       29s
    ✓ 3/5  ATS check                 35s
    ✓ 4/5  Humanizing             1m 22s
    ✓ 5/5  Final check            1m 28s
  Saved resume to ./Ada_Lovelace_Resume_Acme_Corp.md

nextloom doc generate cover-letter app_a1b2c3 --format pdf

  Generating cover-letter for app_a1b2c3 (job job_y1z2x3)...
    ✓ Queued                          1s
    ✓ 1/3  Matching your profile      6s
    ✓ 2/3  Writing the letter        14s
    ✓ 3/3  Humanizing                25s
  Saved cover-letter to ./Ada_Lovelace_Cover_Letter_Acme_Corp.pdf

nextloom doc generate follow-up app_a1b2c3

  # Follow-ups render only as JSON, and the web app has no download name for
  # them, so this keeps the <doc>-<app-id> form rather than inventing one.
  Generating follow-up for app_a1b2c3 (job job_z1x2y3)...
    ✓ Processing                      6s
  Saved follow-up to ./follow-up-app_a1b2c3.json

nextloom doc generate resume app_a1b2c3 --json

  {"ok":true,"job_id":"job_x1y2z3","output":"/home/ada/Ada_Lovelace_Resume_Acme_Corp.md"}

commands.name: nextloom doc status
commands.description: Prints the status of a generation job. Resume and cover-letter jobs run as a pipeline and also report the step they are on; follow-up and thank-you are single-shot and report status only. Takes the job id printed when generation started — not an application id. Use it to recover after an interrupted run, not as a polling loop: `doc generate` already waits.

args.name: job-id
args.description: Generation job id, as printed when generation started.

examples:
nextloom doc status job_x1y2z3

  status:  Processing
  step:    3/5 ATS check
  entity:  app_a1b2c3

nextloom doc status job_x1y2z3 --json

  {"job_id":"job_x1y2z3","status":"completed","aggregate_id":"app_a1b2c3"}

commands.name: nextloom doc list
commands.summary: Show which documents exist for an application.
commands.description: Lists the four document types and whether each has been generated, with the formats each can be downloaded as. Same information as `app view --docs`.
examples:
nextloom doc list app_a1b2c3

  ✓ resume          md, json, docx, pdf
  ✓ cover-letter    md, json, docx, pdf
  — follow-up
  — thank-you

nextloom doc list app_d4e5f6

  No documents generated yet for this application.
  Create one with: nextloom doc generate resume app_d4e5f6

commands.name: nextloom doc get
commands.description: Downloads a document that has already been generated, in any format that type supports. This does not regenerate: it costs no AI quota and leaves the stored document untouched. Fails if the document does not exist yet — generate it first. Resumes and cover letters support md, json, docx, and pdf; follow-ups and thank-you notes are json only.

args.name: type
args.description: Document type: resume, cover-letter, follow-up, or thank-you.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Output format. Resume and cover letter: md, json, docx, pdf. Follow-up and thank-you: json. Defaults to the type’s primary format.

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Where to save the file. Defaults to the name the web app would give it.

examples:
nextloom doc get resume app_a1b2c3 --format pdf

  # no regeneration, no quota — the server renders the stored document
  Saved resume to ./Ada_Lovelace_Resume_Acme_Corp.pdf

nextloom doc get cover-letter app_a1b2c3 --output ./cl.md

  Saved cover-letter to ./cl.md

nextloom doc get resume app_a1b2c3 --format json --json

  {"ok":true,"type":"resume","format":"json","output":"/Users/you/Ada_Lovelace_Resume_Acme_Corp.json"}

nextloom doc get resume app_d4e5f6

  nextloom: no resume has been generated for app_d4e5f6 yet. Create one with: nextloom doc generate resume app_d4e5f6

nextloom doc get follow-up app_a1b2c3 --format pdf

  nextloom: unknown format "pdf" for follow-up. Supported: json

commands.name: nextloom completion shell
commands.description: Prints a completion script for the given shell.  Pipe to `source` or save to your shell's completions directory.

args.name: shell
args.description: Target shell: bash, zsh, or fish.

examples:
nextloom completion shell fish

# fish completion for nextloom — drop in ~/.config/fish/completions/nextloom.fish

complete -c nextloom -l help -d 'Show help'
...

exitCodes.description: Usage error — an unknown command, missing argument, or bad flag.
A document generation job failed or timed out. The job may still finish server-side — check it with generate status.
Not signed in, or the stored session could not be refreshed. Run auth login again.
